latest_nl_proof:
Fix an integer n > 1 and an integer m with 0 <= m <= n-1. By the definition of F_n, for any real x,

F_n(x) = floor(n x) - sum_{k=1}^n floor(k x)/k.

Substitute x = m/n. Then

F_n(m/n) = floor(n(m/n)) - sum_{k=1}^n floor(k(m/n))/k.

Since n(m/n) = m and m is an integer, floor(n(m/n)) = floor(m) = m. Therefore

F_n(m/n) = m - sum_{k=1}^n floor(k m/n)/k,

which is exactly the desired identity.

statement_nl: Let n be an integer greater than 1, and define F_n(x) = floor(n x) - sum_{k=1}^{n} floor(k x)/k. For every integer m with 0 <= m <= n-1, F_n(m/n) = m - sum_{k=1}^{n} floor(k m/n)/k.

domain_restrictions: n is an integer with n > 1
x is a real number (or at least a value for which floor(n x) and floor(k x) are defined)
k ranges over integers from 1 to n (so division by k is valid since k is nonzero)
m is an integer satisfying 0 <= m <= n - 1
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For every integer n with n > 1, define F_n on real x by F_n(x) = floor(n times x) minus the sum over integers k from 1 to n of floor(k times x) divided by k. Then for every integer m with 0 <= m <= n - 1, F_n(m divided by n) equals m minus the sum over integers k from 1 to n of floor(k times m divided by n) divided by k.
